title: Copy complete buffered short spool fields directly
question: Can an admitted buffered field copy avoid redundant zero-fill/read_exact work while preserving strict spool decoding?
summary: Adopt the behavior-preserving fast path after both opposite-order primary elapsed/total-CPU pairs and the frozen practical elapsed rule pass. Scope remains the small native development cell.

workloads: One million plain probe-v1 pipeline rows, fixed seed, four workers and 32-MiB job/shared limits.

validation.summary: Six complete jobs independently preserve fields, unique IDs, groups, strict caps, CSV/output records, seventeen logical Analysis fields and cleanup. Recorded measured-head Linux/browser/Windows local workflows pass; final changed commit/base requires fresh gated delivery.

limitations: Two primary observations per variant and uncontrolled warm cache/background do not establish general device, workload, scale or tail performance.
The ordered negative control also favors the candidate; it does not exercise packed decoding and exposes uncontrolled variation.
Total process CPU benefit is in kernel time; user CPU is flat/mixed. No function attribution, new RSS, physical-I/O or whole-Run peak-capacity claim.
exclusions: Ordered controls and derived summaries are not primary observations and are not pooled or subtracted.
Failed preparation/schema preflight attempts remain failures; no experimental build or Run occurred before their separately retained correction.
Earlier rejected SIMD and empty-grant experiments remain closed; no tuning, repeated jobs or shape expansion.
